met_analysis:
The Low-Pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood persisted over same region at 0830 Hrs IST of today, 25th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation now extends upto 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height.
The Low Pressure Area over Northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal-North Odisha coasts now lies over Northwest Bay of Bengal & adjoining West Bengal Coast at 0830 Hrs IST of today, 25th July, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level. It’s likely to meander over the same region and become more marked during next 2-3 days.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Jaisalmer, centre of Low-pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood, Sheopur, Datia, Siddhi, Daltonganj & centre of Low pressure area over Northwest Bay of Bengal & adjoining West Bengal Coast thence southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level. An east-west shear zone embedded with cyclonic circulations associated with the above two Low Pressure areas, runs roughly along 24°N Lat. across central India between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The trough from cyclonic circulation associated with the Low-Pressure area over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood to Jammu division across West Rajasthan, Punjab between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The offshore trough at the mean sea level from Gujarat to Karnataka coast has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
